title: aham brahmasmi
tomorrow: dearer than a child, dearer than money. what could that be?

segments.voice: Yesterday, aham brahmasmi and an argument inside Advaita: practice it until it's direct, or hear it and see what already is. Today, three pictures of where the self is.

Pick up a pencil case, a closed jar, a matchbox. Give it a shake: something's in there, and you can't see it. A few lines before aham brahmasmi, the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad reaches for objects just like that. A razor, folded away in its case. Fire, asleep in a piece of wood. Footprints in soft ground. Each one answers a question: where is the self, and why is it so easy to miss?
screen: `SOMETHING INSIDE, UNSEEN.` → `A RAZOR. FIRE. FOOTPRINTS.` → `WHERE IS THE SELF?`

segments.voice: The text says the self has entered into all this, right to the tips of the fingernails. It's there the way a razor is there in its case, or fire in the wood it sleeps in. You can hold the case and never see the blade. You can hold the log and never see the flame. Then the text says why people miss it. They see it in pieces. When it breathes, they call it breath. When it speaks, voice. When it sees, the eye; when it hears, the ear; when it thinks, the mind. These, the Upanishad says, are only names for what it does. Whoever holds on to just one of them doesn't know it whole. So: know it as the self, for in the self all these become one. And then the third picture. This self, the text says, is the footprint of everything, because by it one knows everything, the way someone finds what was lost by following its tracks. That's a striking turn. The self isn't one more thing to go and find. It's the trail everything else is found by. And aham brahmasmi says that this same self, in the case, in the wood, on the trail, is Brahman.
screen: `TO THE TIPS OF THE FINGERNAILS.` · `A RAZOR IN ITS CASE, FIRE IN WOOD.` · `BREATH, VOICE, EYE: ONLY NAMES.` · `THE FOOTPRINT OF EVERYTHING.` · then, large: `THE TRAIL ALL ELSE IS FOUND BY.`

segments.voice: Hold one closed thing near you: a box, a jar, a book. Feel its weight and its edges with your eyes open, and know there's something in it you can't see. Then turn the same attention to the hand holding it, all the way to the fingertips.
Aham brahmasmi, and where its self is: in everything to the fingertips, like a razor in its case, and the trail all else is found by.
The line to keep: aham brahmasmi, hidden in plain sight like fire in the wood. That's day 1747.

screen: `DAY 1747 COUNTS.` → `AHAM BRAHMASMI · 4 OF 8.` → `TOMORROW: DEARER THAN A CHILD. WHAT COULD THAT BE?`

chat.meaning: The Brihadaranyaka says the self is in everything like a razor in its case or fire in wood: present all along, unseen until known.

sources.ref: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.4.7 (the self entered here to the tips of the nails, as a razor in its case or fire in its source; breathing it is called breath, speaking voice, seeing the eye, hearing the ear, thinking the mind: these are only names of its acts; whoever worships one of these does not know; it should be known as the self, for in it all these become one; this self is the footprint of all this, for by it one knows all this, as one finds by footprints)
